description: Words a canonical name may use besides the WordNet 3.1 lemmas: the function words that join the words of a phrase, and technical terms WordNet does not list, each with the reference that defines it and its parts of speech.

functionWords.description: Conjunctions, prepositions and articles; a phrase may use them between its words but never as the head of a concept.

terms.definition: A grammar symbol that a rule rewrites into other symbols.
terms.source: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools, 2nd edition (2006), section 2.2.1

terms.definition: Text marked as deleted by a horizontal line through it.
terms.source: GitHub Flavored Markdown Spec 0.29, section 6.5 Strikethrough (extension)

terms.definition: Placed within a line of text rather than as a separate block.
terms.source: CommonMark Spec 0.31.2, section 6 Inlines

terms.definition: The status of being a state.
terms.source: Merriam-Webster Dictionary, statehood (noun)

terms.definition: The period during which a program or parser executes.
terms.source: Merriam-Webster Dictionary, run-time (noun)

terms.definition: To record the state of something at one moment.
terms.source: Merriam-Webster Dictionary, snapshot (verb)

terms.definition: A plain text table format whose records are lines of fields separated by commas.
terms.source: RFC 4180, Common Format and MIME Type for Comma-Separated Values (CSV) Files (2005), section 2

terms.definition: A text that lists the line differences between two files, as the diff utility writes it.
terms.source: POSIX.1-2017 (IEEE Std 1003.1-2017), diff utility

terms.definition: A configuration file format of bracketed sections that hold key and value settings.
terms.source: Microsoft Win32 API documentation, GetPrivateProfileString function (initialization files)

terms.definition: Not enclosed in quotation marks.
terms.source: RFC 4180, Common Format and MIME Type for Comma-Separated Values (CSV) Files (2005), section 2

terms.definition: A datum written with a hash-colon prefix that evaluates to itself and is never a variable.
terms.source: The Racket Reference, Reading Keywords

terms.definition: A template, written with a backquote, whose unquoted parts are evaluated.
terms.source: R7RS small (2013), section 4.2.8 Quasiquotation

terms.definition: A part of a quasiquote template, written with a comma, that is evaluated.
terms.source: R7RS small (2013), section 4.2.8 Quasiquotation

terms.definition: A syntax template, written with a hash-backquote, whose unsyntax parts are evaluated.
terms.source: The Racket Reference, Reading Quotes

terms.definition: A part of a quasisyntax template, written with a hash-comma, that is evaluated.
terms.source: The Racket Reference, Reading Quotes

terms.definition: A thing of any kind.
terms.source: Merriam-Webster Dictionary, anything (noun)

terms.definition: The character or character pair that ends a line of text.
terms.source: The Unicode Standard, version 15.0, section 5.8 Newline Guidelines

terms.definition: Characters such as spaces, tabs and line breaks that separate tokens and print as blank space.
terms.source: R7RS small (2013), section 2.1 Identifiers and section 7.1.1 Lexical structure

terms.definition: The part of a declaration that names what it declares and gives its pointer, array and function structure.
terms.source: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), section 6.7.6 Declarators

terms.definition: The part of an initializer that names the member or element it initializes.
terms.source: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), section 6.7.9 Initialization

terms.definition: The expression or brace-enclosed list that gives an object its initial value.
terms.source: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), section 6.7.9 Initialization

terms.definition: The translation phase that runs directives and expands macros before a program is parsed.
terms.source: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), section 5.1.1.2 Translation phases and section 6.10 Preprocessing directives

terms.definition: Enclosed in parentheses.
terms.source: Merriam-Webster Dictionary, parenthesize (verb)

terms.definition: Taking a variable number of arguments.
terms.source: ISO/IEC 14882:2020 (C++20), section 13.7.4 Variadic templates [temp.variadic]

terms.definition: Not guaranteed to sit at the alignment its type requires.
terms.source: Microsoft C/C++ language reference, __unaligned

terms.definition: The company whose compilers define the Microsoft-specific C and C++ syntax.
terms.source: Microsoft C/C++ language reference, Microsoft-specific modifiers

terms.definition: Otherwise; the branch taken when a condition fails.
terms.source: Merriam-Webster Dictionary, else (adverb); ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), section 6.8.4.1 The if statement

terms.definition: Metadata at the start of a source file, set off by lines of three or more dashes.
terms.source: RFC 3503, frontmatter; The Rust Reference, Frontmatter

terms.definition: A name in a macro matcher that binds a fragment of the input for the transcriber.
terms.source: The Rust Reference, Macros By Example, Metavariables

terms.definition: The ::<> syntax that gives generic arguments in an expression path.
terms.source: The Rust Reference, Paths, Paths in expressions

terms.definition: A placeholder that matches anything, such as the _ pattern or the * of a glob import.
terms.source: The Rust Reference, Patterns, Wildcard pattern

terms.definition: Qualified by the path of the module, type or trait that contains it.
terms.source: The Rust Reference, Paths, Qualified paths

terms.definition: A fixed-length ordered sequence of values of possibly different types.
terms.source: The Rust Reference, Tuple types

terms.definition: Under which conditions; a where clause states the bounds a generic item requires.
terms.source: Merriam-Webster Dictionary, where (adverb); The Rust Reference, Generic parameters, Where clauses

terms.definition: Binding the parts of an array or object value to the names of a pattern.
terms.source: ECMA-262 16th edition (ECMAScript 2025), section 13.15.5 Destructuring Assignment

terms.definition: An XML-like syntax extension of ECMAScript whose elements and attributes describe a tree of components.
terms.source: JSX specification (facebook.github.io/jsx), Draft: JSX Specification

terms.definition: Describing the running program itself rather than a value it computes, as new.target and import.meta do.
terms.source: ECMA-262 16th edition (ECMAScript 2025), section 13.3.12 Meta Properties

terms.definition: The object a module namespace import or export binds, whose properties are the exports of a module.
terms.source: ECMA-262 16th edition (ECMAScript 2025), section 16.2.2 Imports (NameSpaceImport) and section 10.4.6 Module Namespace Exotic Objects

terms.definition: The keyword that evaluates to the receiver of the current function call.
terms.source: ECMA-262 16th edition (ECMAScript 2025), section 13.2.1 The this Keyword

terms.definition: Written without an escape sequence, as the plain characters of a string literal are.
terms.source: ECMA-262 16th edition (ECMAScript 2025), section 12.9.4 String Literals

terms.definition: Built from another type by applying one transformation to each of its property keys, as a TypeScript mapped type is.
terms.source: TypeScript Handbook, Type Manipulation, Mapped Types

terms.definition: Built into the language rather than declared by a program, as the TypeScript primitive types number, string and boolean are.
terms.source: TypeScript Language Specification 1.8, section 3.8.1 Predefined Types

terms.definition: Able to be read but not assigned after initialization, as a TypeScript readonly property or array is.
terms.source: TypeScript Handbook, Object Types, readonly Properties

terms.definition: A type whose values are the values of another type that satisfy a predicate, written {x : α // p x} in Lean.
terms.source: Theorem Proving in Lean 4, section Structures and Records; the Lean 4 core library, structure Subtype in Init/Prelude.lean

terms.definition: Accepted without a proof, as a Rocq proof that Admitted closes is.
terms.source: Rocq Reference Manual, section Proof mode, Admitted

terms.definition: The side, left or right, to which an infix operator groups when it repeats without parentheses.
terms.source: Rocq Reference Manual, section Notations, Simple factorization rules and associativity

terms.definition: A recursive definition by structural recursion, as the Rocq command Fixpoint declares.
terms.source: Rocq Reference Manual, section Recursive functions, Fixpoint

terms.definition: Allowed to be bound implicitly by generalization, as the Rocq command Generalizable Variables declares.
terms.source: Rocq Reference Manual, section Implicit generalization

terms.definition: The tactic language of the Rocq prover.
terms.source: Rocq Reference Manual, section Ltac

terms.definition: A tactic that takes tactics and combines them, such as repeat, try or progress.
terms.source: Rocq Reference Manual, section Ltac, tacticals

terms.definition: To turn off a flag or an option, as the Rocq command Unset does.
terms.source: Rocq Reference Manual, section Flags, options and tables, Unset

terms.definition: Worked out by the compiler instead of written in the source, as the types of the parameters of the Java lambda expression (x, y) -> x + y are.
terms.source: The Java Language Specification, section 15.27.1, Lambda Parameters

terms.definition: Written without annotations, as a Java type with no type annotations before it is.
terms.source: The Java Language Specification, section 8.3, UnannType

terms.definition: An escape in a regular expression that matches the text an earlier capturing group matched, as \1 or \k<name> does.
terms.source: ECMA-262, ECMAScript 2024 Language Specification, section 22.2.2.7.2, BackreferenceMatcher

terms.definition: An assertion of a regular expression that the text after the current position matches, (?=...), or does not, (?!...), without consuming it.
terms.source: ECMA-262, ECMAScript 2024 Language Specification, section 22.2.2.4, Assertion

terms.definition: An assertion of a regular expression that the text before the current position matches, (?<=...), or does not, (?<!...), without consuming it.
terms.source: ECMA-262, ECMAScript 2024 Language Specification, section 22.2.2.4, Assertion

terms.definition: A lookahead or a lookbehind: an assertion of a regular expression about the text around the current position that consumes none of it.
terms.source: Jeffrey E. F. Friedl, Mastering Regular Expressions, 3rd edition (2006), chapter 2, Lookaround

terms.definition: The Portable Operating System Interface, the IEEE standard of the interfaces of Unix-like systems, whose regular expressions name character classes as [:alpha:].
terms.source: POSIX.1-2017 (IEEE Std 1003.1-2017), Base Definitions, section 9.3.5, RE Bracket Expression

terms.definition: The character encoding standard that assigns a code point and properties to every character of the world's writing systems.
terms.source: The Unicode Standard, Version 15.1 (2023), chapter 1, Introduction
